questions.question_html:
Recent studies suggest that $12%$ of the world population is left handed. Depending on parents' hand usage, the chances of having left handed children are as follows:
A: Both parents are left handed, chances of having left handed children $=24%$
B: Both parents are right handed, chances of having left handed children $=9%$
C: Father left handed and mother right handed, chances of having left handed children $=17%$
D: Father right handed and mother left handed, chances of having left handed children $=22%$
Given $P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=P(D)=1/4$ and L denotes child is left handed. What is the probability that $P(A|L)$ ?
questions.explanation_text: We need to find $P(A|L)$ , which means: Probability that both parents are left handed, given that the child is left handed. Using Bayes’ theorem, $P(A|L)=\frac{P(A)P(L|A)}{P(L)}$ Here, $P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=P(D)=\frac{1}{4}$ Also, $P(L|A)=24%=\frac{24}{100}$ Now find $P(L)$ using the total probability formula: $P(L)=P(A)P(L|A)+P(B)P(L|B)+P(C)P(L|C)+P(D)P(L|D)$ Substitute the values: $P(L)=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{24}{100}+\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{9}{100}+\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{17}{100}+\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{22}{100}$ Since $\frac{1}{4}$ is common, $P(L)=\frac{1}{4}(\frac{24+9+17+22}{100})$ $P(L)=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{72}{100}$ Now, $P(A|L)=\frac{\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{24}{100}}{\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{72}{100}}$ Cancel the common factor $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{100}$ : $P(A|L)=\frac{24}{72}$ $P(A|L)=\frac{1}{3}$ So the correct option is: $\frac{1}{3}$ Option C.

Now, $P(A_{1})=\frac{70}{100}=\frac{7}{10},P(A_{2})=\frac{30}{100}=\frac{3}{10}$ $P(\frac{E}{A_{1}})=$ Probability that a standard quality car is manufactured in plant $X=\frac{80}{100}=\frac{8}{10}$ $P(\frac{E}{A_{2}})=$ Probability that a standard quality car is manufactured in plant $Y=\frac{90}{100}=\frac{9}{10}$ $P(\frac{A_{1}}{E})=$ Probability that a standard quality car has come from plant $X$ $=\frac{P(A_{1}) \times P(\frac{E}{A_{1}})}{P(A_{1}) \cdot P(\frac{E}{A_{1}})+P(A_{2}) \cdot P(\frac{E}{A_{2}})}$ $=\frac{\frac{7}{10} \times \frac{8}{10}}{\frac{7}{10} \times \frac{8}{10}+\frac{3}{10} \times \frac{9}{10}}$ $\begin{aligned} & =\frac{7 \times 8}{7 \times 8+3 \times 9} \\ & =\frac{56}{56+27}=\frac{56}{83} \end{aligned}$ Hence, the required probability is $\frac{56}{83}$ .

$P(\frac{E}{A_{2}})=$ Probability that a standard quality car is manufactured in plant $Y=\frac{90}{100}=\frac{9}{10}$

$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{7 \times 8}{7 \times 8+3 \times 9} \\ & =\frac{56}{56+27}=\frac{56}{83} \end{aligned}$

Hence, the required probability is $\frac{56}{83}$ .
